summary.intent: Rewrite Callisto's 0.19.0 changesets so each user-visible change is clearly communicated to users (upgrading, scripting, setting up), and fix the underlying process and the courier plugin so the problem doesn't recur.
summary.outcome: Agreed on a layered changeset shape (lead line, audience sections, bullets, no hard length caps, one entry per outcome). Ran courier:changeset-analyzer on #483 and found its caps and semver table conflict with that shape. Wrote a detailed hand-off prompt for plugin changes and created a worktree for it. Started rewriting the changeset set (changelog-grouped-layout.md modified), but the rewrite is not yet reviewed by a fresh-context agent.

repo: Callisto changesets are the only release text users read. Entries should name the visible thing, why it helps, and any action required, using `Breaking:` / `Action:` markers.
Fixes to features unreleased in 0.19.0 should get no changeset. This cut 13 entries to 7 and led to dropping #485's changeset.
PRs #483 and #485 both edit one paragraph in docs/architecture/versioning.md, so the second to merge needs a conflict fix.

wisp-plugins: the courier plugin reaches shared/ through a plugins/courier/shared -> ../../shared symlink. The installed Claude cache copy (courier/3.0.3) appears to have no shared/ directory, so load_first references may not load for any plugin.

courier:changeset-analyzer is built around the changeset@2 schema, which has summary.maxLength 200 and 'one sentence for minor / one clause for patch' rules. This is incompatible with layered entries.
The semver table in shared/references/delivery/changesets.md only covers agents, skills and schemas, with no rows for CLI flags, output formats or serialized files.

The wisp-plugins repo requires signed commits, `just check`, `just marketplace-sync` for generated Codex output, version/CHANGELOG bumps via `just versions`, and a byte-identical constitution block in agents.
workflow: The agent had a memory saying to route changeset, commit and PR text through the courier agents, yet wrote them freehand all session. Check available plugin agents before drafting such text.
Rushing to rewrite files without first agreeing the goal repeated the same mistake. Align on goals and outcomes before editing when the user signals quality concerns.
The user rejects prescriptive length targets for LLM output and prefers principles and judgment, plus examples, over hard limits.
The user finds Claude hooks too heavy for reinforcing plugin use, so reinforcement should come from sharper skill trigger wording and README guidance.
Before shipping, a fresh-context agent should read the draft changesets as a first-time user would, and the rendered release PR body should be read before merging.
Subagent hand-back reasoning fields are not forwarded, so limitations placed there are lost.

friction: The agent's repeated changesets were windy, mechanism-focused, and never named the feature (for example, the link in #483), and the user had to correct this several times.
The user was frustrated that the plugin agents weren't being used at all.
The user interrupted a rapid rewrite and an EnterWorktree call, asking instead for a hand-off prompt.
The courier agent's load_first path (shared/references/delivery/changesets.md) did not resolve in the worktree and had to be searched for.
The agent's 200-character cap forced it to drop the direct-push limitation and the scripting detail from its output.
Edits cannot be handled by the agent until the plugin is updated, so the changesets are drafted manually in the meantime.
open_items: Finish the rewrite of the 0.19.0 changeset set (changelog-grouped-layout.md and the others) and have a fresh no-context agent review them as a user would.
The PR #486 description and its seven entries still need the user's review, along with #483 and #485. Rewritten text from this session still has to be reconciled with the layered shape.
Resolve the versioning.md conflict between #483 and #485.

Plugin changes in wisp-plugins, being handled by another agent: remove the length caps, allow layered summaries, add outcome-level granularity, why-it-matters and action requirements, CLI semver rows, and update downstream consumers, tests and versions.
Investigate and report whether Claude installs lose the shared/ symlink.
Update AGENTS.md in Callisto with a concrete changeset shape and before/after examples. Consider adding a PR template 'Changelog' line and a highlights tier, which are the user's decisions.
Section names (What you see, Scripting, Upgrading) are undecided: convention or free-form.
Optional soft lint for changesets in Callisto is undecided.
Unused worktree feat/layered-changesets in wisp-plugins; the user should reuse or delete it.
